title: Understanding the Data Pipeline knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Samples, labels, and batches” in this lesson?
options: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
questions.answer_key: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.
questions.explanation: Samples, labels, and batches: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Dataset versus DataLoader”, what should a learner verify?
options: Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
verify `__len__`, `__getitem__`, sample/label alignment, batch shapes, and that no held-out examples leak into training.
questions.answer_key: verify `__len__`, `__getitem__`, sample/label alignment, batch shapes, and that no held-out examples leak into training.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify `__len__`, `__getitem__`, sample/label alignment, batch shapes, and that no held-out examples leak into training.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Training, validation, and test sets”?
options: Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not shuffle or split features and labels independently; their indices must remain aligned.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
questions.answer_key: Do not shuffle or split features and labels independently; their indices must remain aligned.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not shuffle or split features and labels independently; their indices must remain aligned.
